analysis.article_5_text: Processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner (“lawfulness, fairness and transparency”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: Any processing... should be lawful and fair... transparent... clear and plain language be used.

relevant_clauses.text: This privacy policy (the “Privacy Policy”), together with our Terms & Conditions at ada.com/terms-and-conditions, our Cookie Policy at ada.com/cookie-policy and any other documents referred therein, sets out the basis on which any personal data we collect from you, or that you provide to us, will be processed. Please read this Privacy Policy carefully to understand the types of data we collect from you, how we use it, the circumstances under which we will share it with third parties, and your rights in relation to your personal data.

This Privacy Policy applies to any personal data processed by Ada Health GmbH (HRB 189710), Neue Grünstraße 17, 10179 Berlin, Germany being the data controller (as defined under Article 4(7) GDPR) of all processing activities in connection with the Services.

Before starting using our Services, you should read our Privacy Policy carefully. In order to use our Symptom Assessment and other health related features, you have to consent to Ada analyzing the personal health data you voluntarily share in order to be provided with an assessment and health advice.
Which personal data we may collect and process, why and for how long (detailed in subsections with types of data, purpose, use justification including legal bases, and storage duration).
Your data subject’s rights (detailing rights under GDPR).
Any changes we make to our Privacy Policy in the future will be posted on this page, and where appropriate, notified to you by email, notifications via the App, or by any other available means.

analysis.justification: The policy uses clear and plain language to detail all processing activities, legal bases, and user rights, directly fulfilling Article 5(1)(a)'s transparency requirement by identifying the controller and explaining data handling comprehensively. This aligns with Recital 39's emphasis on lawful, fair, and transparent processing through explicit communication. The structured format and notifications of changes further ensure users are informed, supporting fairness and transparency.

analysis.article_5_text: Collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes (“purpose limitation”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: specific purposes... explicit and legitimate and determined at the time of the collection.

relevant_clauses.text: You are not under any obligation to provide your personal information to Ada. Please note however, that most functionalities rely on information about yourself and specifically your health. Without providing this information you might not be able to use those functionalities at all or to a limited extent.
This section 2 aims at giving you a quick high-level overview of the data processing activities in connection with the Services we provide you.
Which personal data we may collect and process, why and for how long (each subsection specifies types of data, purpose of processing, and ensures no further incompatible processing).
Purpose of processing: When you use the different features of the App or Ada Assess we process your data including your health data to provide you with the requested functionality.
When using Ada’s Services, you are not subject to a decision that is based solely on automated processing which produces legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affects you.

analysis.justification: The policy explicitly lists purposes for each data processing activity in section 3, linking them to legitimate bases like contract performance or consent, which meets Article 5(1)(b)'s demand for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes without incompatible further processing. This specification at collection time aligns with Recital 39's guidance on determining explicit purposes upfront. Restrictions on sharing and anonymization for secondary uses like research ensure compatibility with initial purposes.

analysis.article_5_text: Adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary (“data minimisation”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary... processed only if... could not reasonably be fulfilled by other means.

relevant_clauses.text: You are not under any obligation to provide your personal information to Ada. Please note however, that most functionalities rely on information about yourself and specifically your health. Without providing this information you might not be able to use those functionalities at all or to a limited extent. In some cases, the accuracy of the results might be impacted. This will be indicated in the description of the individual processing activities in Section 3 below.
Each subsection lists specific types of data collected, noting optional fields (e.g., health insurance optional in 3.2a, general health data optional).
The use of this feature is voluntary and not a requirement to use the symptom assessment.
To the extent possible, we use pseudonymized or anonymized data and to perform this task.
We will hold your personal data for as long as it is necessary or required by law or by any relevant regulatory body, and always in compliance with the data minimization principle.

analysis.justification: The policy specifies only necessary data types for each purpose in section 3, with many marked as optional and warnings about limited functionality without them, adhering to Article 5(1)(c)'s limit to what is adequate and relevant. Preference for pseudonymized or anonymized data where possible ensures processing only when purposes cannot be fulfilled otherwise, matching Recital 39's guidance. This approach minimizes collection to essential elements for health services.

analysis.article_5_text: Accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date (“accuracy”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: Every reasonable step should be taken to ensure that personal data which are inaccurate are rectified or deleted.

relevant_clauses.text: When you update information such as height and weight in your profile, we will keep the previous entries to allow you to track its development.

Right to Rectification: As a data subject, you have the right to rectification under the conditions provided in Article 16 GDPR. This means in particular that you have the right to receive from us, without undue delay, the rectification of inaccuracies in your personal data and completion of incomplete personal data.

analysis.justification: The policy enables users to update health profiles and provides a right to rectification without undue delay, fulfilling Article 5(1)(d)'s requirement to keep data accurate and rectify inaccuracies. This mechanism takes reasonable steps for rectification, as guided by Recital 39. For health data, tracking changes supports accuracy in assessments.

analysis.article_5_text: Kept in a form which permits identification … no longer than necessary (“storage limitation”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: period... stored is limited to a strict minimum... time limits... for erasure or... periodic review.

relevant_clauses.text: Each subsection specifies storage duration, e.g., 3.1: Your data is removed after 15 days; 3.2a: until you request deletion; 3.5: corresponds to 3.2a/3.2b, with option to delete specific cases.

We will hold your personal data for as long as it is necessary or required by law or by any relevant regulatory body... If your personal data is used for more than one purpose, we will retain it until the purpose with the longest period expires... After the processing of your data is no longer necessary... we will securely and separately store some of your data in accordance with statutory retention obligations... If the processing of your personal data is no longer necessary for any purpose it is either irreversibly anonymized... or securely erased.
After termination of the account, we will retain your data for up to seven years in secured form... Your data will only be accessed in case of litigation.

analysis.justification: The policy defines strict minimum storage periods for each processing activity in section 3 and overall in section 7, with anonymization or erasure when no longer necessary, meeting Article 5(1)(e)'s limit on identifiable form duration. Time limits and reviews for erasure align with Recital 39's requirements. Retention for legal claims is justified and minimized.

analysis.article_5_text: Processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security (“integrity and confidentiality”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: Any processing... should be lawful and fair... transparent... clear and plain language be used.

relevant_clauses.text: Ada implements a variety of technical and organisational measures to ensure that your data is adequately protected... The implementation of these measures is expressly required by law in Art. 32 GDPR and is also needed for the ISO 27001 certification... Ada also runs bug bounty programs... we conclude a data processing agreement with all third parties involved in accordance with Art. 28 GDPR.

The personal data that we collect from you is stored in the European Union... Sensitive information between your browser and our Website is transferred in encrypted form using Transport Layer Security (“TLS”).

Ada shares your personal data with third parties... who act as our processors based on data processing agreements as required by Art. 28 GDPR... Where we use Service providers who process personal data on our behalf outside the EEA... with the appropriate safeguards... Your health data and other sensitive data will always stay in the EU.
We use the above data... to ensure the proper use, functioning, maintenance and improvement of our Services... as well as to prevent any decompiling or otherwise reverse engineering.

analysis.justification: The policy details technical and organizational measures like encryption, ISO 27001, bug bounties, and DPAs, ensuring security against unauthorized processing as required by Article 5(1)(f). This fair and transparent description of protections matches Recital 39's call for lawful and fair processing. Limiting sensitive data to the EU and safeguards for transfers further demonstrate appropriate security.

analysis.article_5_text: The controller shall be responsible for, and able to demonstrate compliance (“accountability”).
analysis.recital_39_reference: Recital 39 does not address accountability (focuses on Art. 5(1)(a)-(f)). Recital 39 silent on Art. 5(2); evaluate it based on article 5(2).

relevant_clauses.text: Ada Health GmbH... being the data controller... Our data protection officer can be contacted at dpo@ada.com.
Detailed documentation of processing activities with justifications, purposes, and durations.
Implementation of measures required by Art. 32 GDPR... ISO 27001 certification.
Use of processors based on data processing agreements as required by Art. 28 GDPR... appropriate safeguards for transfers.
Rights including access, erasure, with verification processes.
Retention in compliance with principles like minimization.

analysis.justification: The policy demonstrates accountability by identifying the controller and DPO, documenting all processing with legal bases, and implementing measures like DPAs, certifications, and safeguards, as required by Article 5(2). Detailed rights enforcement and retention policies show responsibility for compliance. Verification for rights requests further enables demonstration of adherence.
